# Feature: Run-Scoped Acquisition

## 1. Feature Goal

**ID**: FEAT-050
**Source Plan**: `.spec-lite/plan_task_fidelity.md` (G4, G5, G10; §5 "Changed tool contracts" and "CLI surface"; §6 "challenge pages and search politeness"; §7 "Run-scoped acquisition services" and "Evidence identity has one owner"; §10 FEAT-050 logging; §11 success criteria; §12 items 4, 5, 7)

Give each agentic run one owner for everything it acquires from the web: one search service, one document store, and one shared browser for background page work. Each page is fetched at most once per run and gets a stable evidence ID. A challenge page is never read as content, and a scraped search provider is never hit concurrently or after it has challenged us.

Run `20260925T130634Z-research-e1fd1b9d` shows the cost of having no owner:

- 22 `web_search` calls built 22 providers and logged "selected search provider" 22 times ([`orchestrator.ts:1340-1349`](../../../packages/agent/src/runtime/orchestrator.ts#L1340-L1349)). No object could hold a gate or a breaker. The model issued searches in concurrent pairs, and 11 of 22 failed, every one of them inside a pair.
- One results page was fetched 7 times. Of 30 navigations, 9 went to re-fetches. The URL policy charges navigation before any fetch ([`url-policy.ts:185`](../../../packages/agent/src/runtime/url-policy.ts#L185)), so a re-read costs the same as a new page.
- 48 Chrome processes ran: one per SERP scrape ([`scrape-transport.ts:77-80`](../../../packages/core/src/extraction/search/scrape-transport.ts#L77-L80)) and one per escalated fetch ([`fetcher.ts:137-140`](../../../packages/core/src/extraction/fetcher.ts#L137-L140)). `BrowserFallbackFetcher` ignores its timeout and abort signal and waits for `networkidle2`.
- `web_search` always fetches at least one hit, because `limit` has a minimum of 1 ([`web-search.ts:55-61`](../../../packages/agent/src/adapters/pi/tools/web-search.ts#L55-L61)). There is no cheap discovery query.
- A plain GET of the results page returned HTTP 200 with a 3.7 KB CAPTCHA interstitial. It reached Chrome only because of a size heuristic ([`fetcher.ts:224-238`](../../../packages/core/src/extraction/fetcher.ts#L224-L238)). A challenge page that contains `<main>`, or is larger than 10 KB, is extracted as content and published as a source (G10).

Acceptance requires all of the following:

- Within one run, N reads of a URL (same canonical identity, through `web_fetch` or a `web_search` inline fetch) cause exactly **one** network fetch and charge exactly **one** navigation. Every later read returns `{already_read: "S<n>", title}` with no fetch.
- Every successful read carries a run-wide `source_id` (`S1`, `S2`, …). It is minted once per canonical URL and is the same in `web_search`, `web_fetch`, and `browser_extract` results and in the evidence ledger. This is the **evidence-ID interface** FEAT-051 and FEAT-053 build on, and it lands first (TASK-001).
- `web_search` with `limit: 0` returns titles, URLs, and snippets. It fetches nothing, charges no navigation, and launches no browser beyond the SERP scrape itself.
- Every `web_search`, `web_fetch`, `browser_navigate`, and `browser_extract` success carries `budget: {navigations: "u/l", hosts: "u/l"}`.
- One run resolves its search provider once and logs "selected search provider" once.
- A scraped provider never runs two searches at once, and consecutive searches start at least `minIntervalMs` apart.
- The first challenge from a provider opens a breaker. Every later search in that run returns `SEARCH_BLOCKED` with cause `circuit-open`, makes zero provider calls, and launches no browser.
- All SERP scrapes and fetch fallbacks in a run share **one** lazily launched headless browser. Each use gets its own isolated browser context. The per-call timeout and abort signal are honored. A run launches at most 2 Chrome processes: this pool plus the task controller's own browser when browser tools are used.
- Every fetched response is classified before extraction as `challenge`, `js-shell`, or `content`, from a documented list of generic challenge-widget markers.
  - An HTTP-tier challenge is rendered **once** in the shared browser. This is policy (b), signed off by the user on 2026-10-10.
  - A browser-tier challenge is terminal for that URL: a `blocked` failure with a handoff and a Brief notice, never extracted, and never re-fetched in the run.
  - Both tiers are audited.
- `yantra doctor` warns when only scraped search providers are available, and names the keyed-provider setup command. `yantra init` offers to store a search key.
- FEAT-049's deterministic tier passes with `FEAT-050` removed from `PENDING_OWNERS`.

### Scope and non-goals

In scope: G4's structural politeness (gate and breaker; FEAT-048 owns the classification of causes), G5 in full, G10, the run-wide evidence ID, discovery-only search, the budget meter, and the `doctor`/`init` provider checks.

Out of scope, owned elsewhere:

- Typed `SEARCH_*` codes, `tool_failure` warnings, `RunHealthLedger`, runtime-derived notices, and the `budget` stage (**FEAT-048**). FEAT-050 adds rows and counters to them; it does not rebuild them.
- Page shape, records, links, structured data, tables, and record anchors `S<n>#r<k>` (**FEAT-051**). FEAT-050 mints only `S<n>`.
- Research browsing, the task contract, and prompt `agent-v9` (**FEAT-052**). FEAT-050 changes tool descriptions only where its own contract changes.
- Citations by evidence ID and cited-versus-consulted sources (**FEAT-053**).
- The deterministic `ask` and `research --no-llm` loops keep their own fetch, search, and cache wiring (plan §7). They receive only two things: the honest timeout/abort in `BrowserFallbackFetcher`, and the challenge classifier inside `HybridContentFetcher`, because both live in shared core classes. Their per-use browser launch is preserved through an explicit adapter (TASK-004).
- Soft error pages (HTTP 200 with "not found" text; TODO line 213) are not challenges, and they stay open.
- Falling back to another search provider after a breaker opens is not done; the run reports `SEARCH_BLOCKED` honestly instead (see TODO entry, §6).

## 2. Data Model (Granular)

No relational store. `.spec-lite/data_model.md` does not exist. Everything here is in-memory run state plus additive fields on FEAT-048's `RunHealth` artifact.

### Entities & Attributes

- **`canonicalUrl(raw)`** (core, `extraction/url-identity.ts`; moved from `research/source-pool.ts:normalizeUrl`, which re-exports it): lowercased host, no fragment, tracking parameters stripped, one trailing slash removed from a non-root path, and the default port dropped. It is the one identity function for "same page". FEAT-048's interim normalizer is deleted.
- **`DocumentRecord`** (core, `extraction/document-store.ts`; one per canonical URL that was read successfully):
  - `sourceId` (string, `S<n>`, NOT NULL, UNIQUE, minted in first-success order starting at `S1`)
  - `canonicalUrl` (string, UNIQUE), `url` (string, as first requested), `finalUrl` (string | null, when it differs)
  - `title` (string | null), `fetchMode` (`'http' | 'browser' | 'observed'`), `firstTool` (`'web_search' | 'web_fetch' | 'browser_extract'`)
  - `firstReadAt` (ISO string), `captureRef` (string | null), `reads` (int ≥ 1: the first read plus each repeat served from the store)
- **`FailureMemo`** (core, same module; keyed by canonical URL): `{ code: string, reason: string, failure: unknown }`. It is stored only for **terminal** failures, those that cannot change within the run:
  - HTTP 4xx other than 408 and 429;
  - `too-large`;
  - challenge;
  - content type refused;
  - extraction empty;
  - an ethics robots or blocklist refusal.

  Timeouts, network errors, 5xx, 408/429, rate-limit refusals, and budget refusals are never memoized.

- **`DocumentStore`** (core class; one per run):
  - `read<T>(url, load: () => Promise<LoadOutcome<T>>): Promise<StoreRead<T>>`. It canonicalizes the URL, checks the record index (by requested or final canonical URL), then the failure memo, then in-flight loads (single-flight), and only then calls `load`.
    - `LoadOutcome<T>` = `{ ok: true; value: T; meta: { url, finalUrl, title, fetchMode } } | { ok: false; terminal: boolean; code: string; reason: string; failure: unknown }`.
    - `StoreRead<T>` = `{ kind: 'fetched'; record; value } | { kind: 'hit'; record } | { kind: 'failed'; code; reason; failure; memoized: boolean }`.
  - `observe(url, meta: { title, tool })`: records a page the browser already shows. It mints or returns an ID without any network fetch.
  - `attachCapture(sourceId, ref)`, `get(sourceId)`, `lookup(url)`, `entries()` (in mint order).
  - `stats()`: `{ networkLoads, hits, memoHits, observed }`.
- **`SearchPoliteness`** (core, `extraction/search/search-service.ts`): `{ maxConcurrent: number; minIntervalMs: number }`, taken from a table keyed by the registry descriptor's `kind`:
  - `scrape` → `{ maxConcurrent: 1, minIntervalMs: 2000 }`
  - `api` → `{ maxConcurrent: 2, minIntervalMs: 0 }`

  Values are named constants with a comment citing G4. They are not user config (plan §12 item 7 spirit: re-tune only on harness evidence).

- **`SearchBreaker`** (same module): `{ open: boolean; openedBy: 'anomaly-challenge' | 'rate-limited' | null; openedAt: string | null; skipped: number }`.
- **`SearchService`** (core class; one per run):
  - `resolve(): Promise<Result<SearchProvider, SearchProviderError>>`. It is memoized, including a failed resolution, because configuration cannot change mid-run. The returned provider is a **gated facade** with the same `name`, whose `search()` passes the gate and the breaker.
  - `stats()`: `{ calls, providerCalls, challenges, breakerSkipped, peakConcurrency }`.
- **`SearchCircuitOpenError extends SearchProviderError`** (core, `search/errors.ts`): `context.code = 'circuit-open'`, `openedBy`. It is thrown by the facade with no provider call.
- **`PageSource`** (core, `browser/page-source.ts`): `withPage<T>(fn: (page: Page) => Promise<T>, opts: { timeoutMs: number; signal: AbortSignal }): Promise<T>`.
- **`PagePool implements PageSource`** (core, `browser/page-pool.ts`; one per run):
  - It launches one headless, ephemeral session lazily. Concurrent first callers share the launch promise.
  - Each use gets a fresh **isolated browser context** through `BrowserSession.newIsolatedPage()`, and the context is closed after the use.
  - At most `maxConcurrentPages` (default 2) are open. Waiters queue in FIFO order and honor their abort signal.
  - After a crash or disconnect it relaunches at most `maxRelaunches` times (default 1) per run, then fails typed.
  - `close()` is idempotent.
  - `stats()`: `{ launches, contexts, peakConcurrency, timeouts }`.
- **`launchPerUsePageSource(provider)`** (same file as `PageSource`): today's behavior, one launch per use, preserved for the deterministic `ask`/`research` paths.
- **`BrowserSession.newIsolatedPage(): Promise<Page>`** (core interface addition). `LocalBrowserSession` implements it with Puppeteer `browser.createBrowserContext()` plus `context.newPage()`. The facade's `close()` closes the context. `puppeteer-core` 25.10.0 is already pinned. Every `BrowserSession` fake gains the method (clean break; §3 lists them).
- **`ResponseClass`** (core, `extraction/response-classifier.ts`), a discriminated union:
  - `{ kind: 'challenge'; marker: ChallengeMarker }`
  - `{ kind: 'js-shell' }`
  - `{ kind: 'content' }`

  `ChallengeMarker` is a closed string union of the documented marker IDs (TASK-005).

- **`FetchError.context.kind`** gains `'challenge'`, with an optional `tier: 'http' | 'browser'` and `marker`.
- **`FetchTierEvent`** (core; emitted by `HybridContentFetcher` through an optional `onTierEvent` callback): `{ kind: 'escalated'; reason: 'js-shell' | 'http-error' | 'http-challenge'; host } | { kind: 'challenge'; tier: 'http' | 'browser'; marker; host }`.

### Model-visible contracts (agent tool results)

- `web_fetch` success adds `source_id`, and the middleware adds `budget` (TASK-003).
- `web_fetch` repeat: `ok: true`, `{ already_read: 'S3', source_id: 'S3', url, title, capture_ref?, note }`, with no `text`. `note` is a registered message that says the content was returned earlier as `S3`.
- `web_fetch` of a memoized failure returns the original code and a registered "already attempted this run" message, with `details.already_attempted: true`.
- `web_fetch` challenge: `errorCode: 'SITE_CHALLENGE'`, `retryable: false`, `details: { host, tier, handoff: true }`.
- `web_search` `sites[]` replace per-call `n` with `source_id`. A hit already read is `{ source_id, url, title, already_read: true }`.
- `web_search` with `limit: 0` returns `{ query, mode: 'discovery', results: [{ url, title, snippet }], note }`. There is no `sites` or `failures` field.
- `browser_extract` `content` success adds `source_id`. It never returns `already_read`, because it reads the live page, which may have changed since.

### Protocol changes (additive)

- `RunHealth` (FEAT-048 schema, still `schema_version: 1`). Every new field is optional for readers:
  - `fetches.cache_hits` and `fetches.memo_hits`
  - `fetches.challenges: { http, browser }`
  - `browser.contexts` and `browser.pool_launches`
  - `searches.breaker_skipped` and `searches.peak_concurrency`
- `EvidenceEntry` (agent, internal) gains `sourceId: string | null`. The ledger keeps its own first-seen order. FEAT-053 consumes it.

No Brief schema change. Notices reuse the existing `blocked` and `other` kinds.

### Relationships

- One run has one `SearchService`, one `DocumentStore`, and one `PagePool`, all constructed in `composeDefaultEnvironment` and carried on `RunServices`. The nested `workflow_run` orchestrator keeps its own provider and is out of scope.
- `DocumentRecord` 1:1 canonical URL; 1:1 `EvidenceEntry` when the read reached the ledger; 1:N reads.
- `PagePool` 1:0..(1 + `maxRelaunches`) browser sessions; 1:N isolated contexts.

### Indexes & Constraints

- `sourceId` values are dense and monotonic (`S1…Sn`) with no gaps, because failures never mint.
- `stats().networkLoads` equals the number of `load()` invocations. The harness checks this against the fixture server's request log.
- At any instant, a scraped provider has at most 1 search in flight (asserted from `peakConcurrency`).
- After `close()`, the pool's sessions are all closed and `withPage` rejects with `PagePoolClosedError`.

### TASK-001: Run document store with stable evidence IDs: `web_fetch` reads a page once

- [ ] **Implementation**:
  - **Identity.** Move `normalizeUrl` from `research/source-pool.ts` into `extraction/url-identity.ts` as `canonicalUrl`, and add default-port removal. `source-pool.ts` re-exports it under the old name. Delete FEAT-048's interim `repeat_fetches` normalizer and derive that count from `canonicalUrl`.
  - **Store.** Implement `DocumentStore` (§2):
    - Look up by canonical requested URL **and** canonical final URL, so a redirect target counts as already read.
    - Single-flight: a second `read` of a URL whose load is in flight awaits it and then resolves as `hit`. Only the first caller gets `fetched`.
    - Mint `S<n>` only on a successful load or an `observe`.
    - Memoize only failures where `terminal === true`. `isTerminalFetchFailure(error)` is exported and encodes the §2 list in one place.
    - A load that throws an unexpected error propagates. It is neither memoized nor swallowed (memory → never silently swallow errors).
  - **URL policy split.** `UrlPolicy.evaluate(url)` runs every check except the budget and audits allow/reject as today. `UrlPolicy.reserve(allowed)` charges navigation and host, and returns `BUDGET_EXHAUSTED` with FEAT-048's `budgetLimit`. `check()` is now `evaluate` then `reserve`, and `browser_navigate` keeps calling it, because a navigation always reaches the network.

    - On `hit`: return the `already_read` payload (§2) with no evidence re-add and no rank signal.
    - On `failed` with `memoized`: the original code plus the `already-attempted` message.
  - FEAT-048's `RunHealthLedger.recordFetch` is called from inside `load` only, so it counts real network fetches. Add `recordCacheHit` and `recordMemoHit`.

### TASK-004: One shared headless browser (`PagePool`) for SERP scrapes and fetch fallbacks

- [ ] **Implementation**:
  - Add `BrowserSession.newIsolatedPage()` (§2), implemented in `LocalBrowserSession` with `createBrowserContext()`. Closing the returned facade closes its context. The method throws `BrowserCrashedError` on a closed or crashed session, as `newPage` does. Add the method to every `BrowserSession` fake listed in §3.
  - Implement `PagePool` (§2):
    - **Timeout.** `withPage` races `fn` against `timeoutMs` and the caller's signal. On timeout or abort it closes that context, which cancels in-flight page work, and rejects with a timeout `FetchError` or the abort reason. The slot is always released (`finally`).
    - **Launch.** The pool launches with `{ profile: { kind: 'ephemeral' }, headless: true }`. A launch failure propagates as the typed core startup error, so FEAT-047's `mapBrowserStartupError` still classifies it.
    - **Crash.** On the session's `crashed` or `disconnected` event, the next `withPage` relaunches while launches remain within `1 + maxRelaunches`. Otherwise it throws `PagePoolExhaustedError`.
    - **Logging.** The pool logs `page pool launched` once per process at info level, with the session ID only.
  - Implement `launchPerUsePageSource(provider)`: it launches, opens one page, runs `fn` under the same timeout race, and closes the session in `finally`. This is today's per-call behavior, now with an honest timeout.
  - **`BrowserFallbackFetcher({ pages })`**: the body runs inside `pages.withPage`, with `goto(url, { waitUntil: 'networkidle2' })` bounded by `timeoutMs`. The status rule is unchanged. **`ScrapeTransport({ pages, ethicsGate, logger })`**: the same, with `domcontentloaded`. `SearchProviderDeps.browserProvider` becomes `pages`.
  - **Orchestrator**: construct one `PagePool` from the run's (FEAT-048 counting-decorated) `leaves.createBrowserProvider(...)`. Pass it to both `BrowserFallbackFetcher` and the search deps. Close it in the finalizer through `captureTeardown`, after the controller's teardown and **before** FEAT-048 writes `run-health.json`. The task `AgentBrowserController` keeps its own lazily launched browser. Two reasons:
    1. it may run headed for `do`, and background fetches must never open visible windows;
    2. its page carries the user-visible interaction state, which isolated fetch contexts must neither see nor disturb.

    That gives at most 2 processes per run.

  - **CLI `ask`/`research`**: pass `launchPerUsePageSource(browserProvider)`. Their behavior is unchanged apart from the honest timeout.
  - RunHealth gains `browser.pool_launches` and `browser.contexts` from `pool.stats()`.

    - a crash → 1 relaunch, and a second crash → `PagePoolExhaustedError`;

### TASK-005: Classify every response before extraction, and treat challenge pages as blocked (policy b)

- [ ] **Implementation**:
  - **`classifyResponse(doc)`** in `response-classifier.ts`. It is pure and reads only the HTML already in hand.
    - **Cheap pass.** One lowercase scan for the marker tokens below. No DOM parse happens unless a marker hits (memory → diagnostic work only where needed; asserted by a spy on the parser).
    - **Confirm pass, on a hit only.** Parse once with the pinned `cheerio`, compute the visible text length excluding `script`, `style`, and `noscript`, and return `challenge` when **either** of these holds:
      1. a widget marker is present **and** visible text is under 1,500 characters;
      2. a challenge phrase appears in `<title>` or the first `<h1>`, **and** visible text is under 3,000 characters.

      The size limits stop a long article with an embedded comment-form CAPTCHA from becoming a challenge.

      > **DEVIATION (implementation, 2026-10-11):** a third rule was added — a challenge phrase in `<title>` or the first `<h1>` **and** a widget marker present, at any size. FEAT-049's `challenge-large-main` fixture pads the interstitial with ~12 KB of _visible_ help text, so rules 1–2 alone classify it as `content`, contradicting this spec's own G10 acceptance (the padded `<main>` variant must be a challenge). Requiring both independent signals keeps the two false-positive guards intact: the long article with a comment-form CAPTCHA has no challenge phrase in its heading, and an article _about_ CAPTCHAs has no widget.

    - **Otherwise.** Return `js-shell` when the response is HTML under 10 KB with a script `src` and no `<article>`/`<main>`. This is today's escalation rule moved verbatim. In every other case return `content`.

  - **`CHALLENGE_MARKERS`**, a short documented list with one header comment justifying it under memory's "never write website-specific logic". These are standard, cross-site challenge-**widget** components, in the same category as ARIA roles. They are not a site list, and no host or brand appears:
    - widget attributes and classes: `data-sitekey`, `g-recaptcha`, `h-captcha`, `cf-turnstile`, and a `captcha` token on an `id`/`class`/`name` inside a `<form>`;
    - challenge phrases: "verify you are human", "are you a robot", "unusual traffic", "checking your browser", "press and hold", "complete the security check".

    Each marker has a stable `ChallengeMarker` ID. The list carries a comment that `SITE_TOKEN_SOURCE` must stay clean against it (FEAT-049's lint list).

  - **`HybridContentFetcher`**:
    1. HTTP fetch → classify.
    2. On `challenge`: emit `{ kind: 'challenge', tier: 'http' }`, then make **one** browser render. This is policy (b), signed off 2026-10-10, and the code says so in a comment citing plan §12 item 4.
    3. On `js-shell`: emit `escalated/js-shell`, then render.
    4. On an HTTP error or network failure: emit `escalated/http-error`, then render, as today.
    5. Classify the browser document. On `challenge`: emit `{ kind: 'challenge', tier: 'browser' }`, then throw `FetchError` with kind `challenge`, `tier: 'browser'`, and `marker`.
    6. A browser `js-shell` is returned as content. A second render would not help, and FEAT-051 reports shape and coverage.

    The browser path never retries, never waits for a challenge to clear, and changes nothing about the browser's identity (plan §6).

  - **`processSource`**: a challenge `FetchError` becomes stage `blocked`, with reason `challenge page (<marker>)`. That produces a `blocked` rank signal, which is correct: the site's own bot detection refused us.
  - **`web_fetch`**: a challenge returns `SITE_CHALLENGE` (§2) with the registered message. It says the site served a human-verification page, that the run cannot and will not pass it, and to use evidence from other reads or `result_publish` saying the page was blocked. Its capability is `result_publish`. The handoff detail means an unpublished run ends as a handoff. The challenge is memoized through `isTerminalFetchFailure`, so a re-call costs no fetch.
  - **Audit and notices.** The orchestrator passes `onTierEvent` into the run's fetcher.
    - Each `challenge` event writes one `warn` `{ event: 'fetch_challenge', tier, marker, host }` to `runtime.jsonl`. Each `escalated` event writes one `info` `{ event: 'fetch_escalated', reason, host }`. Payloads carry no URL path or page text.
    - `RunHealthLedger` counts `fetches.challenges.{http,browser}`.
    - Notice derivation adds one `blocked` notice per host whose browser tier was challenged. It also adds one `other` notice per host whose HTTP tier was challenged but whose browser render succeeded: "`<host>` refused Yantra's HTTP client with a human-verification page; the page was read once in the standard browser."

- [ ] **Unit Tests**:
  - Classifier fixtures. Each is a nameable generic pattern, and no fixture contains a real site token:
    - small interstitial with `data-sitekey` → `challenge`;
    - the same padded past 10 KB **and** wrapped in `<main>` → `challenge` (pins G10);
    - phrase-only interstitial → `challenge`;
    - a 4,000-word article with a comment-form `g-recaptcha` → `content`;
    - script shell → `js-shell`;
    - plain article → `content`.
  - Parser spy: 0 parses on a marker-free page.
  - `HybridContentFetcher`:
    - HTTP challenge + browser content → returns the browser document and emits `[challenge/http, escalated/http-challenge]`;
    - HTTP challenge + browser challenge → throws `FetchError` kind `challenge`, tier `browser`, with exactly 1 browser fetch;
    - js-shell → 1 render;
    - content → 0 renders.
  - `processSource`: a challenge → stage `blocked`.
  - `web_fetch`:
    - `SITE_CHALLENGE` with `handoff: true`, no evidence entry, and not in provenance;
    - a re-call → 0 fetches;
    - the message passes the hint-capability contract test.
  - Notices: one `blocked` and one `other` notice are derived as specified, and the `runtime.jsonl` lines pass FEAT-048's forbidden-data scan.

### TASK-006: One search service per run, with a politeness gate and a challenge breaker

- [ ] **Implementation**:
  - **`SearchService`** in core (§2). The constructor takes `{ resolve: () => Promise<Result<SearchProvider, SearchProviderError>>, logger, now, sleep }`. The resolver is the FEAT-049 `resolveSearchProvider` leaf with the run's deps bound, so the scripted harness provider is gated exactly like a real one.
    - `resolve()` is memoized, so "selected search provider" is logged once.
    - **Gated facade.** `search(query, opts)`:
      1. If the breaker is open, throw `SearchCircuitOpenError` immediately: no provider call and no wait.
      2. Otherwise wait for a slot under `SEARCH_POLITENESS[kind]`. Waiting honors `opts.signal`, and an abort while queued rejects with the abort reason and makes no provider call.
      3. Wait until `minIntervalMs` has passed since the previous provider call **started**.
      4. Call the provider.
      5. If the error is `ScrapeSearchError` with code `anomaly-challenge`, or a `RateLimitError`, open the breaker, log one `warn` `{ event: 'search_breaker_open', provider, cause }`, and rethrow the original error so that FEAT-048 maps this first call to `SEARCH_BLOCKED` with its true cause.
    - Every other error passes through untouched and never opens the breaker.
    - The kind comes from `SEARCH_PROVIDER_REGISTRY[provider.name].kind`.
  - **`search-errors.ts`** (FEAT-048): add the row `SearchCircuitOpenError` → `SEARCH_BLOCKED`, `retryable: false`, cause `circuit-open`. It has its own registered message: search is closed for the rest of this run because the provider challenged an earlier query; `web_fetch` a URL from an earlier result, or `result_publish` and say search was blocked. FEAT-048's distinct-message test covers it.
  - **Agent wiring.**
    - `SearchToolDeps` becomes `{ service: SearchService; resultCap; fetchTop }`.
    - `web_search` calls `deps.service.resolve()` and uses the facade.
    - The orchestrator constructs one service per run. `composeDefaultEnvironment` no longer calls `resolveSearchProvider` per tool call.
    - `RunHealthLedger` reads `service.stats()` at teardown for `searches.breaker_skipped` and `searches.peak_concurrency`.
    - FEAT-048's notice table gains a phrase for `circuit-open`: "`<n>` later searches were not attempted after the provider's challenge."

## 6. Cross-Cutting Concerns

- **Auth**: N/A. The `init` search-key step reuses the existing keychain path, and the key never reaches the agent. Browser contexts are ephemeral and isolated, and none carries user cookies.
- **Security and ethics**:
  - A challenge page is never extracted, never a source, and never retried in a loop.
  - The browser render after an HTTP-tier challenge is the user-approved policy (b). It is audited at both tiers and disclosed in a notice, and it uses the standard browser with no identity change.
  - Serializing a scraped provider and stopping after its first challenge is how the run honors that provider's rate limiting. There is no UA rotation, proxying, or fingerprint change (plan §6).
  - The URL policy's checks are unchanged. Splitting `evaluate` from `reserve` moves only _when_ navigation is charged, and policy still runs before the store, so a refused URL never reaches a cached answer.
  - `UrlProvenance` recording is unchanged. Discovery results are attested exactly as `more_results` were.
- **Error handling**:
  - Typed core errors throughout: `SearchCircuitOpenError`, `FetchError` kind `challenge`, `PagePoolClosedError`, `PagePoolExhaustedError`.
  - Store loads that throw unexpectedly propagate, are never memoized, and reach the middleware's generic handler.
  - Every new tool message names only engineered moves (`web_fetch` of an attested URL, `result_publish`) and declares its capability (memory → Coding Standards).
  - The pool always releases its slot and context in `finally`.
- **Logging** (Pino JSONL to `runtime.jsonl`; no URL path, query, or page text):
  - `selected search provider`: once per run.
  - `page pool launched`: once per pool process, at info.
  - `search_breaker_open`: warn, once.
  - `fetch_challenge`: warn, per tier and host.
  - `fetch_escalated`: info.

  FEAT-048's `run_health` gains the counters in §2.

- **Diagnostic cost**:
  - The classifier's cheap pass is one string scan, and it parses only on a marker hit (spy-asserted).
  - The meter reads an in-memory snapshot.
  - The store adds one map lookup per read.
- **Compatibility**:
  - `RunHealth` fields are additive and optional. Old run directories render unchanged.
  - Tool result shapes change (`n` → `source_id`, plus `budget`), which internal pre-release contracts permit. No user-owned artifact format changes.
  - The deterministic `ask`/`research` paths keep a per-use browser through `launchPerUsePageSource`.
- **Enhancement tracking** (appended to `.spec-lite/TODO.md` during implementation):
  - Whether the deterministic `ask`/`research --no-llm` loops should adopt `SearchService`/`DocumentStore`/`PagePool` (plan §7 defers it).
  - Whether a breaker-open run should fall back to the next provider in the `auto` chain, which today never has a keyed provider behind a scraped one.
  - Whether the task controller and the pool should share one process when the run is headless.
